reasons: the paper's own subject-level test reproduces exactly: it reports T+ = 313, N = 28, p = 0.011; recomputing the Wilcoxon signed-rank on the same 28 dogs from the raw parquet gives W = 93, hence T+ = max(W, N(N+1)/2 - W) = 313 (match: True) and p = 0.0110 (match to 3 dp: True) | every route agrees at alpha on those 28 dogs: paired t p = 0.0204, Wilcoxon p = 0.0110, sign test p = 0.0357, sign-flip permutation p = 0.0119; incongruent minus congruent = 141.6 a.u. claim_short: looking times did not differ cong vs incong
reasons: the non-difference reproduces on the paper's own DV: it reports chi2 = 0.12, df = 1, p = 0.731 for trial type on the proportion of dwell time, and the subject-level contrast recomputed here is -0.0075 (95% bootstrap CI -0.0414 to 0.0264), all routes p >= 0.68 | in the interpretable unit the paper uses for its descriptives, the same contrast is -3.8 ms on a congruent mean of 4189 ms (95% CI -459 to 419 ms, permutation p = 0.991) | CAVEAT: the interval admits differences up to about 11% of the congruent mean, so the data are consistent with a null but do not establish one; the paper states no smallest effect of interest and reports no equivalence test, and its bootstrap CIs are in Table S2, which was not supplied | automatic proposal: supported

claim_short: gaze transitions did not differ cong vs incong
reasons: the non-difference reproduces: incongruent minus congruent = 0.066 transitions on a congruent mean of 2.20; all routes p >= 0.60 | the 95% bootstrap interval runs -0.38 to 0.46 transitions, about +/-21% of the congruent mean; consistent with a null, not an equivalence demonstration | the paper reports chi2 < 0.01, df = 1, p = 0.951 for trial type and chi2 = 2.95, df = 1, p = 0.086 for session number; the subject-level recomputation agrees in conclusion for trial type | 34 of 152 trials contain zero transitions, so the subject-level mean summarises a count with a hard floor at 0 | automatic proposal: supported
